summary: Successful Shorts on competitor channels leverage 'How it's made' engineering visuals and life-or-death scenario explanations. Our channel performed best with concrete gadget mechanics like battery and airplane windows, while abstract 'what if' space scenarios flopped entirely. Moving forward, we will pivot to high-stakes 'how it works' mechanical explanations and use high-emotion, punchy Hinglish hooks that highlight a specific mystery or dangerous misconception.
do_more: Visualize the internal mechanics of household objects (e.g., how an elevator or ATM works)
Use high-contrast visual transitions every 2-3 seconds to maintain audience retention
Incorporate a 'scary or mind-blowing' truth about everyday items early in the video
Focus on manufacturing processes or hidden automation that people use daily but don't understand
avoid: Abstract space, cosmic, or hypothetical scenarios (e.g., 'What if the moon vanishes')
Slow-paced educational intros that define terms before getting to the mystery
Over-explaining science concepts; focus on the impact or the 'how' instead
Using vague or broad titles that don't name the specific object being discussed
hook_tips: ATM machine note count karte waqt wo aawaz kahan se aati hai? 😱

title_tips: Start with the specific object + 1 power word like 'Sach' or 'Secret'
Add a high-stakes emotional trigger like 'Darr jaoge' or 'Shocking Truth'
Keep titles under 60 characters for maximum mobile visibility
